subject: Private deployment: BYOK controls & operator visibility questions

Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — BYOK and operator access

Hi Naomi / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week. Before procurement can move forward we need to confirm a few privacy/ops points for our private deployment (on-prem with a dedicated VPC):

1) We plan to hold customer keys (BYOK). Can you confirm whether Redwood ever holds an unencrypted copy, or if there is an operator breakglass that could decrypt customer data?

2) What subprocessors will have access to telemetry/logging for the private deployment? We need a list and the specific types of telemetry retained.

3) Are there any automatic cross-border transfers of logs or telemetry (we are US-based but have EU patients)?

We have an internal security review next Tuesday — if you can provide a short written note and any evidence (SOC2 excerpts / audit logs example) that would help.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lopez
Security & IT, Acme Therapeutics
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — BYOK and operator access

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by attachments and a proposed MAP: 

- Keys: Redwood does not retain an unencrypted copy of customer CMKs when BYOK is selected. Customers manage the primary key material in their KMS. Nursery: we support both KMS integrations (cloud KMS) and an on-prem HSM connector.

- Operator breakglass: We offer an operator breakglass process for emergency decrypts, but it is gated:
  * Requires written customer approval and two internal approvers (legal + security),
  * Each event is time-limited, logged, and submitted as an evidence package to the customer.
  * For customers that require zero-operator-decrypt guarantees we can include a no-breakglass addendum (see redline).

- Telemetry/subprocessors: Attached is a redline of the DPA that includes an appendix listing subprocessors and telemetry categories. By default, operator telemetry (health metrics, scheduler traces, kernel telemetry) is retained for 30 days and is obfuscated; customer data and prompt/response payloads are not logged unless telemetry explicitly flagged for debug and with consent.

- Cross-border: Our control plane is configurable. For private/on-prem deployments we can restrict control-plane egress to US regions only; any evidence access can be routed over a customer-controlled VPN. We document the transfer flows in the DPA annex.

I've attached a redline (redline_privdep_dpa_acme_v1.docx) and proposed MAP with milestones for evidence delivery and procurement. Proposed next step: review the redline today and we can set a 30-minute call Monday to walk the security team through the breakglass and telemetry controls.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman

Adding a technical perspective. Key points for the security review: 

1) BYOK model: In our integration the customer KMS issues ephemeral wrapping keys to the Redwood gateway. The gateway uses the wrapped key to encrypt the local keystore; the unwrapped material is held in-memory only on the GPU host and never written to disk. This means Redwood operators cannot obtain a persisted plaintext key under normal ops.

2) Breakglass design options:
  - Standard: breakglass via customer-signed approval + internal approvals; offers forensic logging and escrow of the session token.
  - Strict: no operator decrypt — we can insert a contractual clause that requires the customer to manage all decryption operations. In that setup we provide tooling (transfer APIs and operator-run playbooks) but we will not initiate decrypts.

3) Telemetry: we categorize logs as:
  - Operational (host CPU/GPU metrics, scheduling, queue times) — retained for 30 days by default, aggregated and pseudonymized.
  - Platform traces (errors/exceptions, model faults) — retained 90 days for debugging and root cause.
  - Customer payloads (prompts/responses) — not stored unless explicitly enabled for debugging; if enabled, it is encrypted under the customer key and scoped by time window.

I've attached an ops matrix that maps subprocessors to telemetry types; this should help the procurement/security team see who gets what level of access.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Sara — small follow-up and proposed MAP to keep procurement to the 9/22 target. Responses below and next steps.

1) Breakglass evidence sample: Attached in the Drive link (see related_links). Sample contains: approval chain, timestamped session log, decrypted object fingerprint, and post-event forensic dump. We'll redact customer payloads in the example.

2) Subprocessors geography: We maintain a definitive subprocessors list in the DPA appendix. Monitoring vendors that touch low-level host telemetry are US-only by default for your proposed deployment; any EU-hosted telemetry vendors are only used if the customer explicitly opts in to long-term remote telemetry storage. We will add a clause to ensure no automatic EU transit without prior written consent.

3) Timeline & MAP: Proposed milestones —
  - 9/08: Finalize redline and sample evidence package (we'll deliver the sample by EOD).
  - 9/12: Security walkthrough (30 min call).
  - 9/16: Legal review complete and final redlines exchanged.
  - 9/22: Signed DPA + SOW.

If that looks good I'll book the 9/12 slot and upload the sample evidence to the shared Drive. If procurement needs any additional artifacts (SOC2 report excerpt, escalation contact list) let me know and we'll include them in the package.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.
Naomi
